newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BRIERLEY SETS J/V WITH CAMERLIN.
newsitem.headline: BRIERLEY SETS J/V WITH CAMERLIN.

text.p: Brierley Investments Ltd said on Thursday it had formed a joint venture company -- BIL Camerlin Ltd -- with Malaysian-based Camerlin Group Berhad. Brierley will own 70 percent of the company and Camerlin will own 30 percent.
The initial capital of BIL Camerlin will be US$150 million - of which US$105 million will be subscribed by Brierley and US$45 million by Camerlin.
Malaysian-listed Camerlin Group Berhad's principal shareholders are Hong Leong Group (Malaysia) HLPB.KL , 27.58 percent, Renong Group RNGS.KL , 12.35 percent, and Camerlin BVI Ltd, 22.23 percent.
Camerlin BVI is an investment consortium, whose shareholders are Singapore's First Capital Corp, Sembawang Corp SEMS.SI , Haw Par Brothers International Ltd HPAR.SI , and KMP Private Ltd.

Brierley said that since Camerlin acquired 20 percent of its equity in March 1996, the company had worked closely with consortium members, particularly the Hong Leong Group Malaysia, to explore ways in which the value of the new relationship could be maximised to the mutual benefit of both groups.

"BIL Camerlin will draw on the respective strengths within Asia of the consortium members, who are now Camerlin shareholders, and Brierley's own extensive international investment skills," the company said.
"It is anticipated that BIL Camerlin's investments will primarily be in listed equities in the Asian region and in companies outside the region where value can be added in an Asian context."

Initial directors of the joint venture will be Paul Collins, Bob Matthew, Andrew Meehan and Rodney Price representing Brierley, and Tan Sri Quek Leng Chan, Chan Wing Leong and Rosie Gan Hui Tin representing Camerlin.
BIL Camerlin's chairman will be Tan Sri Quek Leng Chan.
The company will initially be administered from the Brierley regional office in Hong Kong, which will also continue to manage Brierley's existing Asian assets.
Tan Sri Quek Leng Chang said the changing dynamics of the regional markets provided new opportunities for a value investor combining the complementary skills of its shareholders.
"The company has already identified a number of opportunities and sees an exciting future," he said.
